scenario.title: Environments, release flows and approval gates
situations: Stage promotion or parallel target QA
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
scenario.review: Older research may describe heavier onboarding. Apply minimum activation and optional-adoption boundaries first.
questions: Serving-runtime support and each actual project definition still require live validation; no deployment was executed in this audit.

lessons.title: Use the project topology
lessons.when: Delivery is being configured or changed
lessons.need: Name actual environments and final delivery target. A persistent flow has one declared final target; richer stages can name other registered targets. Neither two environments nor stage-before-prod is universal.
lessons.surface: Flow target contract; stage reference validator; target-specific QA rules.
lessons.gap: Current managed onboarding still gives stage/prod creation and first-stage-deploy recipes. Proposed teaching should derive names/order from the project rather than copy Yoke topology.

lessons.title: Validate the executable route
lessons.when: Before activation, assignment or changing a release policy
lessons.need: Read the serving validation result, capabilities, registered targets and deployed-identity proof. Current source supports ordered execution and scoped QA; a stored definition is not evidence the serving build can execute it.
lessons.surface: Onboard validate gate; flow schema and identity admission.
lessons.gap: JOURNEYS needs a short validation/recovery pointer at the moment a flow is adopted. Used definitions are versioned and retained, not overwritten.

lessons.title: Know who is deciding what
lessons.when: Authoring a release approval or receiving its request
lessons.need: Release human-approval is distinct from a QA verdict. Review exact run/stage, declared reviewers and any/all policy. One approval may still leave others outstanding; cleared approval wakes the same run driver.
lessons.surface: approve skill lines 17–58; deployment-runs approve help.
lessons.gap: Concept exists and execution has a home; the delivery setup journey should offer this choice when defining release risk rather than leave users to discover stage JSON.

lessons.title: Recover the same run
lessons.when: Run waits, is interrupted or refuses target occupancy
lessons.need: Read the named holder, current stage and structured refusal. Runs occupy target origins until QA settles; a live driver owns re-entry. Recover the existing run using its printed command rather than duplicate it.
lessons.surface: Delivery rules opening and run records.
lessons.gap: Expose one recovery link from the human run page and agent result. Never export Yoke self-deploy db-admin authority as an ordinary project requirement.
